newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House of Representatives honors Mother Teresa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House of Representatives honors Mother Teresa.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives voted unanimously on Tuesday to make Mother Teresa an honorary U.S. citizen for her work on behalf of the poor and sick in India and around the world.

"Mother Teresa is a living saint. She has worked tirelessly for the sick and dying," Representative Michael Flanagan, an Illinois Republican, said before the 405-0 vote. The bill now goes to the Senate for final action.

The Roman Catholic nun, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979, founded the Missionaries of Charity in 1949. It runs 544 homes for unwanted children and the destitute in more than 80 cities. The work includes caring for nearly 7,000 children in 120 homes and arranging 1,500 adoptions each year.
In Calcutta, doctors said Mother Teresa, 86, was alert and cheerful as she recovered from a fall on Monday.

"Mother Teresa's general condition is stable. She is alert and cheerful, there is no neurological deficit and she is being kept under observation," a medical bulletin issued by Calcutta's Woodlands Nursing Home said.
Doctors said a suspected spot had been found on her brain, but that there was no cause for alarm.
She had been admitted to the same hospital on Aug. 20 with heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia. She was released 18 days later and told to rest in bed.

Only four other individuals have been granted honorary U.S. citizenship by Congress: Winston Churchill, Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg, and William Penn and his wife Hannah, who helped found the state of Pennsylvania.
